name: Cardio / zone 2 for leanness

lead: Zone 2 cardio is steady, conversational-pace aerobic exercise, commonly placed at roughly 60 to 70 percent of maximum heart rate. People use it to burn calories and lower body fat, aiming for a leaner face and body without hard training that cuts into lifting recovery.

At this intensity fat is the main fuel, and sources report that aerobic exercise promotes weight loss, with fat loss being a whole-body result of energy balance rather than targeted to one area. Public-health bodies recommend about 2.5 hours of moderate aerobic exercise a week for health. High-intensity intervals can deliver similar benefits in less time, and zone 2 has no universally accepted definition.

paras: People walk briskly on an incline, cycle, row or use an elliptical for 30 to 60 minutes several times a week, often on non-lifting days or after training. It is combined with a calorie deficit and strength work. Body-fat changes build over weeks to months.

Reported risks include overuse injury, overtraining, and low-energy-availability problems in high-volume athletes who under-fuel. People with heart conditions or who are new to exercise are commonly advised to build up gradually.

angle.text: Users do steady low-intensity cardio to burn calories and lower body fat, which brings a leaner face and body into view. Aerobic exercise is well studied for health and weight, and zone 2 specifically for leanness is still debated.

lead: Cardio for leanness is the use of aerobic exercise, including low-intensity steady-state work often called zone 2, to lose body fat and look leaner. Zone 2 has no universally accepted definition but is commonly placed at roughly 60 to 70 percent of maximum heart rate, where fat is the main fuel and lactate is cleared about as fast as it is produced.[1]

Public-health bodies recommend about 2.5 hours of moderate aerobic exercise per week for health, and sources report that aerobic exercise promotes weight loss.[2] Encyclopedic sources note that aerobic exercise also has other benefits, and that high-intensity interval training can deliver similar benefits in less time.[2]
infobox: About 60-70% of max heart rate (varies by model)
Clinical trials on zone 2 for leanness

paras: Aerobic exercise is sustained activity such as running, cycling, swimming or walking that relies mainly on aerobic energy production.[2] Zone 2 training is a low-intensity form in which slow-twitch muscle fibers and fat oxidation do most of the work, and it is claimed to raise mitochondrial density and fat oxidation, allowing higher power at the same heart rate.[1]

At low intensity the body relies mostly on fat for fuel, and faster glycogen use takes over as intensity rises.[2] Proponents in fitness communities say this makes zone 2 an efficient fat-burning zone. One encyclopedic source states that low or moderate intensity is less efficient for fat loss than high intensity, though that section carries a verification flag, and it attributes fat reduction to lipolysis across the body rather than to fuel burned during the session.[2]
Research cited on spot reduction reports that exercise does not selectively remove fat from trained areas, so facial leanness is understood to follow overall fat loss.[3]
Overuse injuries, overtraining syndrome, and relative energy deficiency in sport in athletes with high training volume and low intake are reported risks of aerobic training.[2]

Evidence is limited to general aerobic-exercise literature: a 2023 dose-response meta-analysis linked more physical activity with lower cardiovascular disease, cancer and mortality.[2] A 2025 narrative review in Sports Medicine assessed zone 2 training and mitochondrial capacity, but its findings were not summarised in the sources reviewed.[1] No studies found specifically on zone 2 for facial leanness.
